incumbent.name: Jack Rosa
incumbent.summary: Jack Rosa, a Republican, won the open Starke County sheriff's seat in November 2022 with about 54% of the vote, succeeding Sheriff Bill Dulin, and has served since 2023 {abc57_2022} {starke_2022_general}. He is seeking a second term in 2026 {wkvi_cands_2026} {wkvi_primary_2026}.
record: November 2022: Elected sheriff with 54.16% of the vote over Democrat Kelly Fisher (34.14%) and independent Dennis Fornelli (11.69%) {starke_2022_general}.

2023–2025: According to WKVI's summary of the office's 2023–2025 report released by Rosa in January 2026, the office created a Strategic Response Team in 2023 targeting methamphetamine, fentanyl and heroin; launched an anonymous tip line; and credits joint work with the prosecutor, coroner, federal agencies and neighboring counties with a 55% drop in overdose deaths in 2024 and a 60% drop in 2025 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

2023–2025: The same report lists more than 6,000 training hours, replacement of patrol vehicles that had rebuilt titles, a State Board of Accounts financial audit the sheriff requested in 2023, an Indiana Sheriffs' Association jail audit completed in 2024, two corporal positions created in 2023 within the existing budget, and a 50% drop in hands-on use-of-force incidents by correctional officers in 2024 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

February 2025: Rosa presented quotes for two 2023-model squad cars totaling $83,292; council members debated whether to pay from CEDIT, Jail CEDIT or the Cumulative Capital Development Fund, and Council President Todd Leinbach cited State Board of Accounts concerns from the prior year in preferring the capital fund. Deputy Chief Wayne James told the council the department has about 18 vehicles and runs two officers per shift {wkvi_squadcars}.

April 2025: County commissioners approved $52,452 from the Cumulative Capital Development fund for computer replacements, pending council approval, with the sheriff to cover any additional cost from commissary funds if necessary {wkvi_commr_apr2025}.
October 2025: Rosa was scheduled to discuss the county's use of metal detectors with commissioners {wkvi_commr_oct2025}.

January 2026: The office reported that a Crime Suppression Team became operational and that a partnership with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Indiana to pursue federal cases would begin in 2026 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

September 8, 2026: Rosa announced the county would not renew its contract with Flock (an automated license-plate camera vendor), citing public opinion and uncertainty about how collected data is used {wndu_flock}.

race_context: Starke County Sheriff Jack Rosa is completing his first term and is eligible to run again; he faces Democrat Brack Rowe in the November 3, 2026 general election {wkvi_cands_2026} {wkvi_election_central}.

In the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, Rosa won a three-way contest with 1,391 votes (55.93%) over Matthew Topelian (571, 22.96%) and Dennis Fornelli (525, 21.11%); Rowe received 522 votes unopposed in the Democratic primary {wkvi_primary_2026}.
Rowe also sought the Democratic nomination for sheriff in 2022, finishing fourth of four with 71 votes (5.24%); Kelly Fisher won that primary {starke_2022_primary} {abc57_2022}.

Recent office-level issues in county meetings have included replacing an aging patrol fleet, which fund pays for vehicles and equipment, and State Board of Accounts concerns raised by council leadership {wkvi_squadcars} {wkvi_commr_apr2025}.
No general-election forum or debate between Rosa and Rowe was found in available coverage.

candidates.summary: Brack Rowe is the Democratic nominee; WKVI identified a Brack Rowe as Starke County's chief deputy in 2013 and as a sheriff's deputy in 2019 {wkvi_rowe_2013_theft} {wkvi_k9_2019}. His current occupation was not found.
background: WKVI identified Brack Rowe as chief deputy of the Starke County Sheriff's Department in December 2013 {wkvi_rowe_2013_theft}.
In February 2015 WKVI reported that the North Judson town council hired Brack Rowe, a Knox native and Indiana Law Enforcement Academy graduate, as a full-time officer {wkvi_nj_2015}.
In August 2019 WKVI identified Brack Rowe as a Starke County Sheriff's Department deputy and K-9 handler who competed in a regional K-9 event {wkvi_k9_2019}.
path_to_ballot: Filed in January 2026 as a Democratic candidate for sheriff {wkvi_cands_2026}; received 522 votes unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wkvi_primary_2026} {in_list}.

Previously announced a run for sheriff in November 2013 for the 2014 primary {wkvi_rowe_2013_announce} and filed for the 2022 Democratic primary, in which he received 71 votes (5.24%) {wkvi_filings_2022} {starke_2022_primary}.
on_incumbent: No statements by Rowe about Sheriff Rosa's record were found in available coverage.
plans: No campaign plans were found in available coverage. When announcing a 2014 run, he said he had a strong vision for the future of Starke County, according to WKVI {wkvi_rowe_2013_announce}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign-finance totals were found in available coverage.
gaps: No campaign website, social-media page, questionnaire or interview for 2026 was found; his stated positions on any office issue are unknown.
His current job and whether he still works in law enforcement were not found.

Background items come from WKVI reports from 2013 to 2019 naming a Brack Rowe; no source explicitly links all of them to the 2026 candidate, though the name, county and law-enforcement career are consistent.
WKVI described him as 'chief deputy' in a December 2013 article and as a 'deputy sheriff' in the November 2013 campaign announcement; the 2014 primary result was not found.
ABC57 spelled his name 'Bracke Rowe' in 2022 coverage; county results and the ballot list use 'Brack Rowe'.

candidates.summary: Jack Rosa is the incumbent Starke County sheriff, first elected in 2022; ABC57 reported in 2022 that his campaign Facebook page cited 35 years in law enforcement {abc57_2022}.
background: ABC57 reported in November 2022 that, according to his campaign Facebook page, he had spent 35 years in law enforcement {abc57_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 55.93% over Matthew Topelian and Dennis Fornelli {wkvi_primary_2026} {in_list}.
In 2022 he won the Republican primary over Gregory R. Wireman with 67.58% {starke_2022_primary}.

items: His office's 2023–2025 report, as summarized by WKVI, describes a focus on high-level dealers, a Strategic Response Team working with the DEA and county detectives, an added detective in 2024 for drug enforcement, and planned federal prosecutions through the U.S. Attorney's Office starting in 2026 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

The report lists a jail audit by the Indiana Sheriffs' Association completed in 2024, cross-training of jail and road deputies in de-escalation and use of force, and mentoring jail staff into patrol positions {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

Has sought county funding to replace patrol vehicles and computers {wkvi_squadcars} {wkvi_commr_apr2025}; the office reported increased proactive patrols in 2024–2025 and Indiana State Police Zone 4 coverage for Starke and Pulaski counties beginning January 2026 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.
The report says the office gave active-shooter awareness training and arranged for deputies to have access to school building layouts {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

Ended the county's Flock camera contract in September 2026, citing public opinion and uncertainty about data use {wndu_flock}; the office's report lists a self-requested State Board of Accounts audit in 2023 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Rosa about his general-election opponent were found.
plans: The office's report listed a Citizens Police Academy and a 'Riding with the Sheriff' program scheduled to launch in February 2026 {wkvi_report_2023_25}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign-finance totals were found in available coverage.
gaps: No 2026 campaign website, questionnaire or interview was found; positions above are drawn from his office's record and report rather than campaign statements.
His career before becoming sheriff (agencies, ranks) was not found beyond the 35-year figure attributed to his campaign Facebook page in 2022.
Overdose-reduction percentages come from the sheriff's office's own report as summarized by WKVI; underlying counts were not reviewed.
The outcome of an October 2025 jail-operations funding request before the commissioners was not found.
